name: agent-fence
description: One permission policy for coding agents. Checks every shell command, file read and write against your .agent-fence.toml rules before it runs, and logs each decision.

interface.longDescription: agent-fence checks each shell command, file read, file write and patch that Codex is about to run against one policy file (.agent-fence.toml in the project, plus your user policy and built-in defaults). Blocked calls come back to the agent with the rule id and the reason; every decision is appended to a local audit log you can read with agent-fence log. The plugin ships a PreToolUse hook and a skill that teaches the agent how to respond to a block. Codex runs a plugin hook only after you trust it in /hooks. Codex hooks cannot prompt, so rules that would ask for approval block with a message telling the agent to ask you. The hook runs the CLI through npx, or a global install is faster. It cannot stop code the agent writes and then runs outside a checked tool call.
capabilities: Checks shell commands, file reads and writes, and patches before they run
Blocks calls your policy denies and tells the agent which rule fired
Logs every decision to a local audit file
defaultPrompt: Explain why agent-fence blocked my last command
Show what agent-fence blocked in this project today
Check whether git push --force is allowed here
